episodes.title: Why AI Makes Team Conflict Harder, Not Easier
episodes.summary: This episode argues that the hardest part of leading modern teams is not managing obvious differences, but surfacing the hidden ones that shape behavior under pressure. Csaba Toth makes a compelling case that culture, personality, and conditioning all interact, but that organizations often mistake stereotypes for understanding. His deeper point is that AI does not remove this problem; it can actually make it worse by giving people more ways to avoid friction, challenge, and self-examination. The executive lesson is straightforward: if you want better decisions, you need more than diversity on paper. You need structured self-awareness, facilitated disagreement, and the discipline to make comfort slightly harder than growth.

episodes.title: A Practical Way to Research Ballot Propositions with AI
episodes.summary: This episode is about decision quality under information overload. Evan Meyer argues that voters do not need more outrage; they need a process. By defining priorities, using AI to research propositions, and checking claims against source material, individuals can make decisions that are more consistent and less reactive. For executives, the lesson is broader: any high-stakes environment benefits from a repeatable framework that turns complexity into judgment.

episodes.title: How to Control AI With Data-First Governance
episodes.summary: Tim Freestone argues that AI is not leveling the playing field; it is magnifying the gaps organizations already had in data management, cybersecurity control, and operational discipline. The real issue is not whether companies adopt AI, but whether they can govern it around specific business outcomes and data controls. Leaders who focus on broad mandates or vanity metrics will create noise, not value. The better path is controlled deployment, domain expertise, and measurable use cases tied to real business inputs and outputs.

episodes.title: How to Build AI Workflows Without Burning Out Your Team
episodes.summary: This conversation is about more than workplace wellbeing. It is a warning to leaders that technology adoption changes the load on people, not just the output of systems. Georgina Woodley argues that AI can accelerate work while quietly increasing pressure, decision fatigue, and organizational friction. The leadership lesson is straightforward: if executives want AI to create durable value, they have to manage the human system with the same discipline they apply to the technical stack.

- **AI changes the risk model:** fast, probabilistic systems can make mistakes at machine speed, so old “critical vs. non-critical” thinking no longer works.

- **Treat AI like a first-class operating force:** the winners won’t just deploy more AI — they’ll govern it with stronger, more scalable controls.
